All — I reviewed Paxion's markup and drafted two alternative redlines for the pricing exhibit. High level guidance first: we should preserve Redwood's right to manage capacity across our fleet, but we can give Paxion specific guardrails that limit immediate reallocation risk without exposing us to unlimited shelf liability.

Option A (notice + limited carveout): insert new paragraph in Exhibit B, section 2 (Reserved Capacity):
"Reserved Capacity Protection: Redwood shall not reassign or reallocate reserved capacity associated with Customer's Order Form for a period of sixty (60) days following written notice to Customer. If Customer's actual utilization falls below the Minimum Commitment for two (2) consecutive Billing Periods, Redwood may provide a written Notice of Intent to Reallocate. Customer shall have thirty (30) days from the date of such notice to cure the utilization shortfall through additional usage, prepayment of capacity, or by providing an updated rolling usage forecast acceptable to Redwood. Reallocation (if not cured) shall be limited to no more than twenty percent (20%) of the Reserved Capacity in any single reallocation event, and Redwood will not reassign capacity to third parties that are in a materially different legal/industry risk class without Customer consent."

Option B (contractual holdout + commitment calendar):
Insert a limited holdout where Paxion may elect, once in the term, to impose a 90-day hold preventing any reallocation so long as Customer provides a 12-month rolling forecast and pays an availability fee equal to 20% of the monthly unused capacity at the current rate.

Washout (true-up):
Propose adding a quarterly smoothing clause: "For purposes of true-up and surcharge calculations, Redwood will compute effective usage on a trailing 90-day average. Surcharges for underutilization shall only apply if the trailing 90-day average is below the Minimum Commitment for two consecutive quarters. Any surcharge will be prorated monthly within the quarter and capped at 10% of the billed amount for that quarter."

Band transitions (caps/floors):
